'''Yu Ruqin''' ({{lang-zh|s=俞汝勤|t=俞汝勤|p=Yú Rǔqín}}; born 21 November 1935) is a Chinese chemist.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://cc.hnu.cn/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=596 |title= Yu Ruqin|newspaper= Hunan University|date=2015 |language=zh}}</ref> He served as [[president of Hunan University]] from 1993 to 1999 and is an academician of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].

==Biography==
Yu was born in [[Shanghai]], but was raised in [[Changsha]], [[Hunan]], his hometown. He secondary studied at [[Yali School]]. He graduated from [[Beijing Foreign Studies University]] and [[Saint Petersburg State University]]. After graduation, he worked at the Institute of Chemistry of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. At the same time, he taught at the [[University of Science and Technology of China]].

He taught at [[Hunan University]] since 1962, what he was promoted to professor in 1980, and served as the university's president from 1993 to 1999.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.library.hn.cn/hxrw/xdrw/keji/yuruqin.htm |title= Yu Ruqin|newspaper=Hunan library |date=2015 |language=zh }}</ref>

In 1991, he was elected a fellow of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. He is a member of the [[Chinese Chemical Society (Beijing)|Chinese Chemical Society]]. He was a member of the 6th, 8th, and 9th National Committee of the [[Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference]].
